recABS9cTyYGHFXEG.Body: The Sonic Slider is the flagship tool behind Biofield Tuning itself, a weighted tuning fork hand-tuned to 93.96 Hz, the twelfth harmonic of the Schumann Resonance, Earth's own natural electromagnetic pulse. Its extended handle lets you glide it smoothly across the face, neck, and body, and practitioners and users regularly report support for relaxation, circulation, and nervous system regulation. It's the same fork Chance uses in his own sessions, and a great entry point if you want to bring this work into your own daily routine.

fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Inner Alchemy and the Podcast Cul-de-Sac", "body": "Chance opens on what he calls the Joe Rogan cul-de-sac, podcasting that feeds seekers just enough before looping them back, and Emily adds that some of it is organic while some, she believes, is orchestrated. Her central view is that the body is a laboratory for alchemy whose inner process mirrors the outer sky clock, and that interest in psychedelics, nootropics, supplements and certain kinds of exercise can be used to steer that inner chemistry. Chance asks whether a true neutral exists, and Emily pictures it as a brief glimpse from a panopticon tower before returning to the chaos."}, {"title": "Alchenomics, Tennis and the Future of Money", "body": "Chance has been reading the late Tracy Twyman's Money Grows on the Tree of Knowledge, which he says frames fiat currency alchemically, with the homunculus as the straw man and turning paper into gold as the real transmutation, and he describes the bigger alchemy as turning our youth into wealth for somebody else. Emily notes her first solo interview was with Twyman and argues money is moving from paper to algorithms. She reads the ATP tennis tour, which shares its initials with the body's energy molecule and with an Atlas Protocol coin she says is meant for smart voting, as a cycle linking body, money and choice."}, {"title": "The Sonic Panoptilectric Frequency Fence", "body": "After Chance recalls a secret online voting project he heard about years ago, Emily argues the system crowdsources solutions from creative thinkers and wants people outside the box, but not too far outside it. She describes a researcher who isolates background radio frequencies in recordings, and Chance coins the sonic panoptilectric frequency fence for this listening sound field. He offers his own view, drawn from Twyman and Keynes, that endless hidden government spending could make large stalking operations plausible, while Emily says the field touches everyone and that a person's own field strength and health decide how sensitive they are to it."}, {"title": "The Watchers and the Conscious Ether", "body": "Chance argues that the panopticon was a spiritual idea long before it was a technological one, pointing to the Watchers, the devil on your shoulder and a Middle Eastern companion spirit said to report back to the demiurge, and he sees little border between secret societies, intelligence agencies and the mafia. Contrasting forest bathing with a humming refrigerator and Wi-Fi left on overnight, he calls dissonance a posture of fear, and suggests the ether is a record of everything and the Watcher itself, which is why we sense no privacy from the higher self. Emily links this to the eyes people describe seeing on mushrooms."}, {"title": "Guardians of the Threshold and I'm Unity", "body": "Emily frames the immune system as pattern recognition, arguing that how healthy you are inside decides how clearly you read patterns outside, and that a settled mind sees the watching eyes as itself or its ancestors rather than as a threat. From dancing to underground electronic music she describes boundary guards, strangers who appear just as the line between realities starts to dissolve, and says getting too far ahead of yourself calls in the guard. Chance shares a group tuning session where one buzzing participant wanted a drink to tamp the energy down, and closes with his reading of immunity as I'm unity."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: Reality Bender, life coach, nutrition guide and Youtube podcaster Emily Moyer joins InnerVerse for a free flow exploration of existential ideas. We delve into technocracy, alchenomics, akashic watchers, targeted individuals, guardians of the threshold, and unity consciousness pattern recognition.
fields.Intro Paragraph 2: In the Plus+ Extension we share our love of underground electronic music culture, ponder the popularity of dissociative identity disorder in media, muse on the multiverse meme, look at the layers of infinite Self, and finish strong on paradoxical particle accelerators, the psychic labyrinth, & much more.

fields.Plus Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Place memory and the Austin that was not there yet", "body": "Emily Moyer describes visions she had after first moving to Austin in 1999 of places that did not exist then but stand there now, and a Los Angeles house party where she kept glimpsing dancers from another era at the edge of her sight. She weighs several explanations, from time travel and remote viewing to the idea that everything that ever happened at a location stays stored there, waiting for someone whose frequency matches. Chance Garton later sums this up as the magic and memory of place, framing it as an open question about how land might hold memory rather than a settled fact."}, {"title": "The multiverse and dissociation in pop culture", "body": "Chance Garton notes a strong push in film and television toward two themes, the multiverse and dissociative identity disorder, pointing to Moon Knight, Loki and the coming Doctor Strange film. He argues these stories frame alternate selves as rivals walled off from us, which he sees as a form of mind shaping. Emily Moyer, fresh from seeing Everything Everywhere All at Once, offers her view of fractal selves as layers of one whole, like colors of a rainbow, and suggests the film shows ordinary people the truth in a form few will believe."}, {"title": "Reality, existence and the coffee that tastes different", "body": "Prompted by a line in the film about coffee tasting different in other realities, Emily Moyer suggests the mistake is assuming we wake into the same reality each day, when in her view we are always moving through slightly different arrangements. Chance Garton offers an etymological angle, arguing that the word reality carries the root real, tied to the king and an external ruler, while existence names the whole. He proposes that people reclaim the word by seeing themselves as sovereign, and Emily welcomes the reframing as a new way of speaking."}, {"title": "Dance, flow states and tuning into a feeling", "body": "Emily Moyer explains that she learned to dance by watching someone's moves at a party and spending the night exploring every variation, then folding that skill away to reopen later. Chance Garton adds that what is really absorbed is the feeling behind the movement, and says he now dances sober with the same intensity because those inner windows stay open. Emily describes repetitive electronic music as ideal for recording a feeling in the body. Chance then traces the word flow through running, rivers, loops and the Latin lupus, noting that wolf reversed spells flow."}, {"title": "Loops, particle accelerators and the speed of time", "body": "Emily Moyer shares her theory, shaped by researchers she follows, that particle accelerators are part of the earth itself, vibrating machines that generate nature, and that one may sit beneath the Austin area she calls the Violet Crown. Chance Garton, drawing on Tracy Twyman's book about money, argues that the velocity of money may act as a lever that speeds up cultural change. Emily ties this to tennis, reading Rafael Nadal's speed, spin and bull symbolism as a small model of world events. Both present these as speculative weavings rather than established findings."}]

fields.Quotes JSON: [{"text": "How you manage yourself is basically the barometer by which you will be managed.", "author": "Emily Moyer", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/ba82a3bc-017a-4ea1-afdb-1e43fdfa532a/EMILY-MOYER.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "When we think about the big picture alchemy that's being done through our bodies, it is this transmutation of our youth into wealth for somebody else.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/aa717e55-9487-4255-a7df-3f8ef10940c4/Chance+Garton+Patreon+Portrait.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "This is a very strange culture around tennis. They literally go in circles and circles and circles around the world the same time every year.", "author": "Emily Moyer", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/ba82a3bc-017a-4ea1-afdb-1e43fdfa532a/EMILY-MOYER.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "I think that the system would like people who are creative thinkers and think outside of the box, but not too far outside of the box.", "author": "Emily Moyer", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/ba82a3bc-017a-4ea1-afdb-1e43fdfa532a/EMILY-MOYER.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "We're afraid of not having privacy because in a sense we know innately that we have no privacy from higher self.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/aa717e55-9487-4255-a7df-3f8ef10940c4/Chance+Garton+Patreon+Portrait.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "How healthy you are on the inside determines how clearly you see the patterns and the perception of things on the outside.", "author": "Emily Moyer", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/ba82a3bc-017a-4ea1-afdb-1e43fdfa532a/EMILY-MOYER.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "You want to have a little bit of reflection and a little bit of anticipation, but if you go a little bit too far in either direction, it's almost like you're calling in the guard.", "author": "Emily Moyer", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/ba82a3bc-017a-4ea1-afdb-1e43fdfa532a/EMILY-MOYER.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "Immunity is I'm unity. That's the ultimate pattern recognition, is I'm unity: I'm unified with the inner, outer world.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/aa717e55-9487-4255-a7df-3f8ef10940c4/Chance+Garton+Patreon+Portrait.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}]
